scenarios.name: enter-from-card-list
scenarios.why: not from the menu: the stored state is not reset, the empty screen is sent with the account id in the card list's default colour

faults.why: 17 on the cross-reference READ -> WHEN OTHER: the file error message
13: an account in the cross-reference but not in the master
19 on the account READ -> the file error message
13 on the customer READ: details stay not fetched
17 on the customer READ -> the file error message

scenarios.name: search-zip-plus4-shown-as-5-digits
scenarios.why: customer 10's ZIP is 44803-4279; the 5-byte screen field shows 44803

scenarios.name: edit-only-case-differs
scenarios.why: names, address and group compare upper-cased: no change detected

scenarios.name: edit-days-blank
scenarios.why: the four day fields cleared: each date 'Day must be supplied', the open date's message shown

scenarios.name: edit-dates-not-on-calendar
scenarios.why: 31 April, 29 February 2025, 30 February 2025, 29 February 1900: refused by the program's own day checks, before CEEDAYS

scenarios.name: edit-dates-valid
scenarios.why: every date passes the program's own checks and reaches CEEDAYS through CSUTLDTC (picture 'YYYYMMDD' plus the two blanks after it in WS-DATE-VALIDATION-RESULT, which EDIT-DATE-LE has just INITIALIZEd); the edit is accepted and PF5 asked

scenarios.name: edit-dob-in-the-future
scenarios.why: date of birth 2030-01-24 passes the program's checks and CEEDAYS, then EDIT-DATE-OF-BIRTH refuses it as in the future (the case clock is 2022)

scenarios.name: edit-signed-amounts
scenarios.why: NUMVAL-C forms: a negative balance, bare integers and a currency sign are all valid, shown re-edited

scenarios.name: edit-zip-leading-zero-refused
scenarios.why: Burlington, VT 05401: the state/ZIP table holds VT50-VT59 (digits 2-3 of 050-059), the program tests digits 1-2 -> 'VT05' refused

scenarios.name: edit-phone-parts-missing
scenarios.why: phone 1 without its area code is refused; phone 2 wholly blank is accepted (optional)

scenarios.name: edit-again-after-errors
scenarios.why: the state the program leaves after a refused edit ('E'): edited again

scenarios.name: enter-again-awaiting-confirmation
scenarios.why: 'N' and ENTER: no edit, no write, the confirmation prompt again

scenarios.name: pf5-account-changed-meanwhile
scenarios.why: the balance shown (350.00) is no longer the file's (400.00): no REWRITE, back to 'S' showing the stale details

faults.why: 19 on the account READ UPDATE -> COULD-NOT-LOCK-ACCT-FOR-UPDATE, state 'L'
19 on the customer READ UPDATE: 2000-DECIDE-ACTION has no WHEN for it -> 'C', 'Changes committed'
17 on the account REWRITE -> LOCKED-BUT-UPDATE-FAILED, state 'F', nothing written
17 on the customer REWRITE -> SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK undoes the account REWRITE, state 'F'

scenarios.name: pf12-rereads-discarding-edits
scenarios.why: 'N' and PF12: the pending changes are dropped, the account and customer read again

notes: CardDemo's account update (transaction CAUP, program COACTUPC), a conversation over several tasks whose state travels in the COMMAREA (ACUP-CHANGE-ACTION and the account and customer details last shown, ACUP-OLD-*, and those typed, ACUP-NEW-*): a search reads the card cross-reference through the CXACAIX alternate index, then the account (ACCTDAT) and the customer (CUSTDAT), and shows both; an edit compares the screen with what was shown and, if anything changed, validates every field (status Y/N, four dates, signed amounts through TEST-NUMVAL-C / NUMVAL-C, SSN parts, FICO 300-850, alphabetic names, city and country, the state code and the state/ZIP combination from CSLKPCDY, North American area codes, EFT id, primary holder Y/N) and asks for PF5; PF5 READs both records FOR UPDATE, refuses if either changed since it was shown, REWRITEs the account then the customer (a failed customer REWRITE is undone by SYNCPOINT ROLLBACK); PF12 reads them again; PF3 SYNCPOINTs and XCTLs back. Each scenario's account and customer files are compared after the task. The scenarios that start mid-conversation set that state as the program itself leaves it (the 'N' state's ACUP-NEW-* are what 1100-RECEIVE-MAP stores from the confirmation screen). Data: the customer and card cross-reference files are CardDemo's own; acctdata.txt here is CardDemo's acctdata.txt with ONE synthetic change -- account 00000000024's ACCT-GROUP-ID (bytes 113-122, blank in the corpus) set to A000000000, the value the corpus puts in the adjacent ACCT-ADDR-ZIP -- because with a blank group id no screen can ever compare unchanged (1100 turns a blank field into LOW-VALUES, compared with the record's spaces), so the 'no change detected' path, PF12 and PF5-before-confirmation would be unreachable. No corpus customer passes the program's own validation (every state/ZIP pair fails the table), so the confirmed edit corrects the ZIP to 66044 (Kansas) and raises the credit limit. Every date the program's own checks accept is passed to CSUTLDTC / CEEDAYS with the 8-byte WS-EDIT-DATE-CCYYMMDD and an 8-byte 'YYYYMMDD' picture, while CSUTLDTC's LINKAGE reads 10 bytes of each: the picture CEEDAYS receives is 'YYYYMMDD' plus the two bytes after it, the first two of WS-DATE-VALIDATION-RESULT, which EDIT-DATE-LE INITIALIZEs (blanks) just before the call, so the blank-tail assumption of register L1 (owner 2026-10-14) covers it with real blanks, not slack; the date's own two extra bytes lie past the picture's span, which IBM ignores. Since #4952 the LE model accepts that picture, so edit-dates-valid reaches CEEDAYS, a valid edit is accepted and the 'S' -> 'N' transition runs, and edit-dob-in-the-future reaches EDIT-DATE-OF-BIRTH. A month outside 1-12 never reaches CEEDAYS (WS-VALID-MONTH refuses it first), so the 2508-vs-2517 refusal stays out of reach here. Defects of the original the scenarios expose: a confirmed update writes ACCT-UPDATE-RECORD, which has no ACCT-ADDR-ZIP, so the group id lands in the ADDR-ZIP bytes and ACCT-GROUP-ID is blanked; a failed customer READ UPDATE (COULD-NOT-LOCK-CUST-FOR-UPDATE) has no WHEN in 2000-DECIDE-ACTION, so the task reports 'Changes committed to database' though nothing was written (and the account stays locked); when either record changed meanwhile the program returns to 'S' but still shows -- and will compare against -- the stale details, not the file's; an account missing from the master (or its file not open) still reads the customer and enters the edit state with zero amounts, because 9000-READ-ACCT tests an 88-level message the NOTFND branch never sets; the state/ZIP table holds digits 2-3 of ZIPs with a leading zero (VT50-59 for 050-059) while the program tests digits 1-2, so a real New England ZIP such as VT 05401 is refused; customer 10's ZIP+4 (44803-4279) is shown in a 5-byte field, so any edit of such a customer is a change and a confirmed one would truncate the ZIP. Branch coverage (2026-10-02): 83 generated scenarios (field-*) each start from edit-no-changes, break one field (blank, a value of the wrong kind, a zero phone part, an area code outside the general-purpose list) or two (the message-already-set branches), with the four day fields cleared; they predate the #4952 CEEDAYS model, which edit-dates-valid now exercises. Their cursor WHENs for fields after the open date stay unreached while the day fields are cleared.
